brief.headline: Global AI Selloff Sparks Tech Correction; Domestic Banks and Power Stocks Rally
brief.summary: Global markets reeled overnight as an AI-driven tech rout pulled the Nasdaq 100 into a bear market and the S&P 500 into correction territory, weighing heavily on global indices. Domestically, the Nifty 50 closed higher at 25800.6, buoyed by strong performances in banking and healthcare while crude prices and US yields eased.

takeaways.text: The Nasdaq 100 plunged 5.6% in its worst week since March 2020 amid surging AI valuation concerns, dragging down global tech and metal markets.
Nvidia shares plunged 14% amid an SEC accounting investigation and executive drama, while Anthropic's blockbuster IPO faced sharp post-debut volatility.
IndusInd Bank surged over 8% on improved business momentum and profitability, leading a resilient domestic market where large-cap breadth stayed positive.
Adani Energy Solutions bagged a major project to supply up to 2,500 MW of renewable energy to West Bengal, boosting green energy prospects.
CrowdStrike is reportedly in acquisition talks with Zscaler, which could mark one of the largest deals ever in the cybersecurity sector.

sections.india: Indian benchmark indices extended their winning streak, with the Nifty 50 closing up 1.12% at 25800.6 and Bank Nifty rising 2.49% to 64635.2. IndusInd Bank and Axis Bank led the banking surge following sequential business improvements, while Voltas entered a joint venture with Atomberg Innovation to manufacture AC compressors. Meanwhile, Ashoka Buildcon lost an ₹846.38 crore Saudi Arabia contract, and Mohan Meakin faced a steep revenue decline due to FSSAI restrictions on Old Monk variants.
sections.world: Global equities suffered a massive correction as fears over AI capital expenditure booms triggered a rout across Wall Street and European bourses. The S&P 500 closed down 3.70% in correction territory, and the Nasdaq tumbled 5.28%. Brent crude fell 2.21% to USD 89.95, while gold dropped 4.62% to USD 3515.4 amidst a hawkish Federal Reserve outlook. US 10-year yields fell 14 basis points to 4.91% and the USD/INR closed lower at 92.67.
sections.tech: Technology sectors globally absorbed heavy shocks from the Anthropic IPO fallout and an ongoing Nvidia sell-off. Nvidia shares fell 14% amid an SEC accounting probe, while Anthropic raised a total of $93.5 billion in its massive market debut. In startup and corporate developments, CrowdStrike entered talks to acquire Zscaler, and an Anthropic researcher claimed to use Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis.

stories.title: Crude prices may normalise to USD 70 by end-2027 as global oil market moves into surplus: Report

Geopolitical tensions, particularly between the US and Iran, are likely to influence oil supply dynamics.
